findings.reason: without a consumer, a green §3 closes the plan while `species`, `breakdown_candidate_grid_point`, `breakdown_candidate_field_line`, `current_alignment`, `plateau` and `green_function` remain absent from the grammar, which is the release's stated purpose for their sources.
findings.text: §3's only outputs are `doubtful-rework.json` and a summary HTML, and `plan-section-depends-on` makes §4 depend on §2 alone, so after this plan completes the six doubtful DD sources are still unnamed and there is no node, followup or dependency that lands the reworked spellings

findings.reason: the guard the section needs is a parse probe on each reworked spelling (round-trip through `parse()` with the reused tokens once §2 has landed, or a recorded unparseable-with-reason), and without it the doubtful six are handed to the lead as reworked while possibly not composing with anything.
findings.text: the node states "No grammar file changes in this section" and its done-when asks only that each row carry a reworked spelling, so a row proposing a spelling that no longer parses with the existing tokens passes

findings.reason: a node following §2 literally would know how to add a YAML token but not where the coordinate-unit rule goes, and the done-when "a name formed with `argmax` carries the coordinate's unit" would be unachievable or would tempt the hand-editing of generated files that the same section forbids.
findings.text: §2 says both `argmax` and `threshold_crossing` need "their unit and rendering rules carried by the grammar", but the named mechanism is only "editing the vocabulary YAMLs and `grammar/specification.yml` and regenerating with `build-grammar`"; `operators.yml` declares `kind`, `precedence`, `returns`, `arg_types`, `separator`, `indexed`, `index_params`, `semantic_effects` and rendering templates — no unit field — while unit and rendering behaviour for names is produced by `grammar_codegen/generate.py` and consumed by the model/renderer, none of which the section names

findings.reason: the segment a node writes to and the form it round-trips (`of_power_convertor` versus a deprecated `power_convertor_<base>` prefix) both depend on this, and the section's representative-name test would otherwise be authored in the deprecated form.
findings.text: the plan places six tokens in "(devices)", which is not a vocabulary: the worklist's `device` rows all carry `yaml_path: imas_standard_names/grammar/vocabularies/locus_registry.yml`, and `specification.yml` declares `- id: device` with `vocabulary: objects` and the authoring note "Retained for parse compatibility only — NOT the preferred authoring form … the postfix-locus convention … is the form enforced by compose tooling"

findings.reason: following the stated substitution would name the intact-pellet density with the shattered-pellet subject, conflating two different DD quantities; the section needs to record that the vocabulary has no intact-pellet species subject and that `species` may be a genuine new token here.
findings.text: §3 asserts "A generic `species` subject is replaced by the named pellet species already in the vocabulary", but the add row's source path is `pellets/time_slice/pellet/species/density` (intact pellet) and the only pellet-species subject in `subjects.yml` is `shattered_pellet_species`, which the worklist already binds to the distinct `shattered_pellet_species_density` reject row

findings.reason: the 35 plain vocabulary tokens are releasable on their own, and separating the two operator semantics lets §4 land the vocabulary while the unit rule is still being worked, instead of holding the whole release on it.
findings.text: §2 bundles a 36-token vocabulary addition with new grammar-level semantics for two operators (`argmax`'s coordinate unit, `threshold_crossing`'s canonical rendering), so one verdict has to close both and §4's release rides on the harder half

rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §3's done-when certifies that a JSON holds one row per doubtful token and that no grammar file changed, but never that a reworked spelling actually composes; §2 and §4 each carry a real measure (§2 additionally carries a planted-removal control).
